segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Hello Mrs. Ramirez. What brings Ethan in to the clinic today?

segments.speaker: Caregiver
segments.text: Doc, he has had a dry hacky cough for 3 days. He does NOT have fever today, although he had a mild warm forehead two days ago.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Has he had any vomiting, diarrhea, or difficulty breathing like wheezing or chest indrawing?

segments.speaker: Caregiver
segments.text: No vomiting, no diarrhea, and breathing seems normal. He is still eating and active.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: What medicines have you given him at home?

segments.speaker: Caregiver
segments.text: We stopped Paracetamol yesterday because he complained of an upset tummy after taking it, and we only gave warm water with honey last night. Does he have any allergies? None that we know of.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Let me listen to his chest. Lungs are clear bilaterally with good air entry, no wheezes or crackles. Throat has mild pharyngeal erythema, tonsils are not enlarged.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: This appears to be an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection. We should hold off on any antibiotics—antibiotics are not indicated here. Continue oral hydration, honey for cough relief, and come back immediately if you notice fast breathing or high fever.
